stories.title: X scraps revenue-sharing program, launches 'Original Content Rewards'
stories.summary: X is ending its long-running ad revenue-sharing program for creators and replacing it with a new initiative called Original Content Rewards. TechCrunch reported the company described the old program as 'misaligned.' Full details on how payouts will work under the new system weren't specified in initial coverage.
stories.whyItMatters: Revenue-sharing terms heavily influence where creators and media accounts choose to post, so a structural change on X could shift creator activity across the social platform landscape.
whatToWatch: How payouts are calculated under the new program
Whether X publishes clear eligibility criteria
Whether creators shift activity to competing platforms
questions: What specifically made the old revenue-sharing model 'misaligned'?
How will Original Content Rewards determine payouts?

stories.title: Planned Amazon data center could become the biggest climate polluter in the US
stories.summary: A planned Amazon data center project could end up as the single largest source of climate pollution in the country, according to TechCrunch. The scale reflects the enormous power demands of AI-driven cloud infrastructure expansion. The report didn't detail the site's location, power source, or specific emissions figures.
stories.whyItMatters: Data centers are increasingly the biggest lever on big tech's carbon footprint as cloud providers race to add AI compute, making this a test case for how the industry squares growth with climate pledges.
whatToWatch: Whether Amazon responds publicly to the projection
What power source ultimately supplies the facility
Any regulatory or community pushback on permitting
questions: What is driving the emissions estimate — the power source, scale, or both?
Has Amazon disputed or confirmed the report?

stories.title: OpenAI acquires presentation startup NextSlide

stories.whyItMatters: Presentations are a core piece of office productivity software; folding NextSlide into OpenAI signals a deeper push into everyday work tools, putting OpenAI in more direct competition with Microsoft and Google's productivity suites.

What happens to NextSlide's existing customers and team
Disclosure of deal terms
questions: What will happen to NextSlide's current product?

stories.title: Census proposal would drop counts of undocumented immigrants, race, and sexual orientation
stories.summary: Wired reports on a proposal that would change how the US Census counts the population — no longer counting undocumented immigrants and dropping data collection on race and sexual orientation. This would mark a significant shift in what demographic data the federal government collects. Who is behind the proposal and its current status weren't detailed beyond the report.
stories.whyItMatters: Census data underpins how companies, researchers, and policymakers model demographics and target resources; removing these categories would ripple into data-driven decisions well beyond government, including in tech and research sectors that rely on that data.
whatToWatch: Whether the proposal advances through any official rulemaking process
Reaction from civil-rights and data-advocacy groups
Any stated timeline for implementation
questions: Who introduced this proposal and at what stage is it?
Would any replacement methodology be used for the removed categories?
